items.author: Alexpakora
items.body:
Follows on from #834 — after working around that one, `caveman claude` starts but every hook (PreToolUse:Skill/Bash/Read) fails:
```
/usr/bin/bash: line 1: C:Users<user>AppDataRoamingnpmcaveman: command not found
```

Root cause: `cavemanBinForHook()` returns `which(caveman)`, a Windows path built with `path.join` (backslash-separated), embedded directly as a hook `command` string. Claude Code appears to execute hook commands via a POSIX shell (`/bin/sh -c`) even on native Windows, which treats `\` as an escape character and strips it — `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\npm\caveman` becomes `C:
items.title: wrap (Windows): hook commands use backslash paths, which git-bash's /bin/sh hook runner strips, breaking every installed hook

items.author: rezachalak
items.body:
\`npx -y github:JuliusBrussee/caveman -- --uninstall\` (and any other flag) fails:
\`\`\`
unknown command "--" — did you mean \`caveman run\`?
see: caveman --help
\`\`\`
That error/help text isn't from \`bin/install.js\` (the installer) — it's from the dependency \`@caveman-ai/cli\`.

**Root cause:** \`package.json\` declares \`"bin": {"caveman": "./bin/install.js"}\`, but \`@caveman-ai/cli\` (listed in \`dependencies\`, v1.2.1) *also* declares \`"bin": {"caveman": "dist/index.js", "cave": "dist/index.js"}\`. When npx installs the temp project, \`node_modules/.bin/caveman\` ends up pointing at
items.title: npx github:JuliusBrussee/caveman -- <flag> invokes the wrong caveman bin (collides with @caveman-ai/cli dependency)
